name: Sternal Cleft

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Sternal Cleft

criteria.description: Visible midline defect or gap in the sternum on physical examination
Radiological confirmation of sternal discontinuity by chest X-ray or CT scan
Assessment to exclude or identify associated congenital cardiac anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of visible sternal gap confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; associated anomalies should be evaluated.

imaging: CT scan confirming sternal cleft and assessing associated anomalies
Echocardiography to evaluate cardiac structure and function
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
Rare familial cases reported with possible autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Physical examination revealing midline chest wall defect
Assessment for associated syndromes such as Cantrell pentalogy

distinguishingFeatures: Complete or partial displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity
More extensive chest wall defect than isolated sternal cleft
Combination of sternal cleft with diaphragmatic and pericardial defects
Presence of abdominal wall defects and intracardiac anomalies

redFlags: Visible cardiac pulsations through chest wall defect
Signs of mediastinitis or chest wall infection
references: Cohen MM Jr. Sternal cleft and related malformations. Am J Med Genet. 1990
Shamberger RC et al. Sternal cleft: diagnosis and surgical repair. J Pediatr Surg. 1990
